newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Bosnia agrees to single currency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Bosnia agrees to single currency.

text.p: Bosnia's collective presidency has agreed to establish a single currency, the State Department announced on Tuesday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the decision came at a meeting in Sarajevo between the three members of the presidency and senior U.S. officials.

"The three (Bosnian) presidents have agreed with the United States on arrangements for establishing a single currency bank, as provided for in the Dayton (peace) accords. This single currency bank will operate as a currency board," Burns told reporters.

"This will establish a single currency in Bosnia-Herzegovina, valid for all transactions. It will be called the convertible marka. It will be linked at a one-to-one basis to the Deutschmark. And it will be fully backed by foreign currency," he said.
Burns called the move "a very important development."

"It means that there will be now a single way to trade and to transact business, and one that is backed by the international financial community. And ... these convertible markas will have a common design, distinct design elements," he said.
